newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary says budget on track despite soc sec gap.
newsitem.headline: Hungary says budget on track despite soc sec gap.

text.p: Hungary is likely to reach its 1997 government budget target despite an unexpected rise in the social security deficit, the Finance Ministry said on Friday.
"There may be small changes in proportions within the government budget, but these will offset each other," Deputy Secretary of State Csaba Laszlo told a news conference.
He said the social security deficit was 21.3 billion forints in March, well above the 13.5 billion forint targeted for the whole year.
Laszlo added that without special measures the deficit could go up to between 40 and 50 billion forints by the end of the year.
"In the case of the health care fund...measures are necessary and probably we cannot avoid making a supplementary budget (for the fund)," he said.

The government is working on plans to reduce the social security deficit and the measures are likely to be aimed at improving the collection of revenues and cooperation with the tax authority APEH, Laszlo said.
The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said on Thursday Hungary's social security deficit was still too high while tax evasion was preventing further reductions.
A government spokesman said on Thursday that the 1997 social security deficit was likely to exceed the target by about 20 billion forints.

Laszlo said there were revenue and expenditure factors which made deficit forecasts difficult, but other sub-systems of the government budget were expected to bring it to the 1997 target of 4.9 percent of gross dometic product (GDP)
"There is a good chance that the central state budget will have a position 20 to 30 billion forints better than planned, and the government funds are also likely to be better," he said.

He added that a planned rise in GDP growth rate to between two and three percent from one percent last year is expected to boost tax revenues and savings can be achieved at public institutions and in government subsidiaries.
Laszlo said the central state budget deficit rose by a relatively small 23.3 billion forints in May to 150 billion forints, mainly due to a lower debt service in that month than earlier in the year.
"For June, a deficit of 40 to 50 billion can be expected, while in both of the two subsequent months the deficit can be 20 to 30 billion forints," he added.
